title: Remember me at the altar (9.11)
hook: dying, Monica asks only to be remembered at the Lord's altar
tomorrow: what is a person actually loving when they love God?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a window at Ostia, and wisdom touched with the whole heart. Your line: for a moment.

A candle in red glass, flickering by a side altar. A name said aloud during the prayers at Mass. Monica's last request is about a moment like that. Not long after the window at Ostia, she falls ill, far from her home in Africa. Friends ask whether she isn't afraid to be buried so far from her own city. Her answer: nothing is far from God, and there's no fear he won't know where to raise her up at the end of the world. Then she tells her sons the one thing she wants.
screen: `A CANDLE IN RED GLASS.` → `FAR FROM HOME.` → `NOTHING IS FAR FROM GOD.`

segments.voice: First, the request. Lay this body anywhere, she says, and don't let the care of it trouble you. Then, in her Latin as Augustine gives it: tantum illud vos rogo, ut ad domini altare memineritis mei, ubi fueritis. This only I ask of you, that you remember me at the Lord's altar, wherever you are. Second, the change. Augustine is surprised. She had long planned to lie beside her husband, and had prepared a grave next to his. Now she lets it go without a fight. Third, what the altar means. For Monica the altar is the Eucharist, and to be remembered there is to be prayed for at Mass. Augustine says that when she was buried, the sacrifice of our redemption was offered for her. Fourth, the turn at the end of book nine. Augustine looks up from the page and speaks to his readers. He asks whoever reads his words to remember Monica and her husband, Patricius, at the altar. So a request made to her sons in a port town is passed to every reader of the book, and that includes whoever is listening now.
screen: `THIS ONLY I ASK.` · `SHE LETS THE GRAVE GO.` · `REMEMBERED AT MASS.` · `PASSED ON TO EVERY READER.` · then, large: `REMEMBER ME AT THE ALTAR.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person who has died, and say their name aloud, softly, once. If you go to Mass, you can carry that name to the altar the way Catholics do; if not, let the sound of the name stay in the room a little longer. If grief is heavy right now, you don't have to carry it alone: in the US you can call or text 988, or reach local emergency help.
Remember me at the altar. Monica's one request as she was dying: not a grave beside her husband, but prayer at the Lord's altar.
screen: `REMEMBER ME AT THE ALTAR — today's word`.

segments.voice: Remember me at the altar: a name, carried to Mass, from wherever you happen to be. Go in peace.

howItsDone: Catholics pray for the dead at Mass, naming them in the Eucharistic Prayer's remembrance of the departed, and a family can ask a priest to offer a Mass for someone who has died.

fork.setup: a friend feels guilty she can't visit her dad's grave across the country. what does Monica's last request offer her?
options: nothing is far from God; remembering him in prayer goes anywhere.
she should move closer, since the grave is what matters most.
remembering only really counts at the grave itself.
fork.reveal: Monica let go of the grave she had prepared. Lay this body anywhere, she said; only remember me at the Lord's altar, wherever you are.

chat.says: back from the visit. Mia's grandma died. her family's not religious. is it weird if i remember her at Mass?
options: Not weird. Monica asked only to be remembered at the altar. Carry her name there, and ask Mia first.
Kind of. Monica says remembering at the altar only works if you're buried near the church.
Skip it. Since Mia's family isn't Catholic, Monica's request means the altar isn't for them.
chat.meaning: Monica let go of the grave she'd planned and asked only to be remembered at the Lord's altar, wherever her sons were. Nothing is far from God.

Monica.meaning: Augustine's mother, honored by the Church as a saint

Eucharist.meaning: the bread and wine of Mass; for Catholics, Christ's body and blood

Ostia.meaning: the port of Rome, at the mouth of the Tiber

notes: Point back: year 3 day 737 told Monica's death briefly; this lesson stays on the request, her change of mind about the grave, and Augustine's appeal to readers in 9.13.37.
Latin quoted from 9.11.27: 'tantum illud vos rogo, ut ad domini altare memineritis mei, ubi fueritis.' Confirm.

'Nothing is far from God ... no fear he won't know where to raise her up' paraphrases 9.11.28 (nihil longe est deo, neque timendum est ne ille non agnoscat in fine saeculi unde me resuscitet). The friends' question and the grave prepared beside her husband are also 9.11.28. 'Not long after the window' avoids the text's count of days.
'The sacrifice of our redemption was offered for her' paraphrases 9.12.32 (sacrificium pretii nostri). Augustine's request that readers remember Monica and Patricius at the altar is 9.13.37.
